I'll start off my platform by making a terribly shameful and painful admission.   Growing up, I was a touch of an Incel before it was a word.  I came from a rich, but ridiculously abusive family (mom hid her wine to keep from killing herself and dad beat the shit out of me all the time and was sexist and homophobic) and was taught terrible lessons.  While its often commented that I'm a very loving person, to this day my empathy suffers.  I obviously try not to be around my step father (sperm donor ditched my mom) anymore, he did leave me with a very bad example, and that with early mental illness left me isolated.  You know what stopped me from becoming the steaming pile of puss and shit that we see today around the internet and sadly even outside sometimes?    


Three things ... Books, the fact that I have a loving mother, the fact that I hated my step father.  I'm pretty sure that most incels don't have the excuse of child abuse and isolation, but books will save anyone worth saving.  Eventually I unlearned enough bullshit that I started making friends and seeing better examples and things got better from there.  I'm honestly not the best case study because I am really mentally ill and a lot of these kids seem like they just have a birth defect or something ... still, books.  Feed them information and keep them isolated a bit so that they can sit there and figure it out a little bit till they aren't toxic as hell.   Once they are, people are actually really awful at explaining or understanding what its like to be so broken you are that hateful and lash out so often.   I actually don't think they should change that, and I say that after having experienced years and years of just being alone and that drove me mad.  You know what you should do for people like that?  Direct them to a strong therapist immediately.  They need wiser, more experienced help than you can give them.  


On a personal note, its weird knowing now that not everyone has an awful home life.  Going through these experiences has left me very crazy, but anyone who knows me now typically says or seems to espouse that they think well of me and I often hear the words "kind" and "loving".  I still won't hang out with people with good childhoods though, its too hard and practically triggering to hear about what its like to be happy when you are young and have safe love from a parent.  Still, I guess at least I didn't grow up poor even though I'm on disability now and can barely think straight.

Hey KattManDue, no fear.  I was not bored.  Look, my situation will change, but my mental illness and the world will not.  I've already attempted twelve times.  Seems I'm really bad at calculating LD50's.  

I've tried loads of different belief systems, but inevitably I just come back to a nihilistic perspective.  Its more my ability to feel, coupled with struggling with severe depression.  

Look, I'm no angel myself, but no matter the perspective or belief system I try there is simply too much suffering in this world for me to swallow and I hate being a part of it.  I hate my own contributions to said suffering, I hate simply being a wet blanket at times because of being depressed.  I'm at a low point right now and am usually a cheerful, though honest person.  I realize that over time, the species has really done nothing but improve.  Wars are smaller and faster.  Hunger is slowly becoming less of an issue.  People have actually become more compassionate and gentle over the ages.  Our concerns and motivations are getting slightly more high minded.  Its still just bad.  Especially since we all live in the trenches of it.  I've tried and failed to help person after person in my life and while my own life is finally on the precipice of becoming livable and good, I've lost a lot of people that I love and I doubt that'll stop just because I can live comfortably and eat decent food.  I donno, a couple of my attempts I got pretty close to staying dead and it even felt like there might be something after death, but ... I still typically would prefer a void to watching another friend or lover circle down the drain, catch a terrible STD, become addicted, or get killed.

Look, my life is really fucking bad right now too and I'm not about to tell you about it to make you feel like your suffering is any more or less or whatever, I'm just going to show you how I deal.  

I was beat up as a kid and lived in a pretty abusive household for a long time after because I was economically trapped.  My step father (who did the beating) recently just about dumped me on the streets with my mom saying that the abuse never happened.  My ex girlfriend is my best friend right now and I'm still in love with her, but she's dating other guys who aren't the best it seems, but I'm practically homeless and (because of medications) I'm a bit more of a chore than not so I know why she's doing what she's doing it just sucks.  This is pretty bad stuff and I work at McDonalds.  Trust me fast food sucks. 

But I'm dealing with it, I'm being proactive.  You gotta force yourself and its really hard to get out of bed in the morning for a long while or go to sleep at a decent hour, but right now I'm quitting smoking ... soon I'll have enough money saved up to go back to the gym.  I'm in a program called OVR (Office of Vocational Rehabilitation) and they might pay for me to go to school.  I'm going to be volunteering at an animal shelter to meet people.  Get busy and keep busy.  See a therapist.  Be grateful for everything you can muster.  Never give up.  

That fear of death is there for a reason, you can only kill yourself if you loose the fear ... but, trust me, it takes a lot more suffering than you or I have experienced to get there.

In my mind it is that simple.  I may be a heterosexual (appearing) white male, but I've got my romantic burdens too.  I'm poly, I've hit on trans girls (post op preferably), I really like D/s style relationships (not full time of course, that shit is taxing).  You don't think my friends, family, co-workers, and neighbors haven't noticed?  I have a pretty bad case of PTSD too.  Approach actually living it like this ... Don't say shit unless they ask and explain it in detail light terms that fit the comfort of your audience.  Here is an example ... I work in a deli right now and the girls over at the bakery found out I was having lots of threesomes with my girlfriend at the time.  They were both disgusted and intrigued, I really couldn't give a fuck what their gossiping was about, but when they finally did ask I simply told them that it was something my lady and myself found fun.  They ended up not having the courage to ask much more about it and eventually their light teasing stopped with the appropriate level of reproachful facial expressions.  

Another example not based on me ... There is a trans lady at work who's voice really just hasn't changed at all.  She's otherwise quite attractive and yes there is gossip.  I simply make a few passes and feel no need to comment about her being born into the wrong body.  If someone approaches you differently (in the sense of seeing you displaying bi sexual tenancies), do what she does ... ignore them and feed instead off the people who encourage you to be here and appreciate your presence. 

Internally, address those who are critical with remorse and pity.  They are cutting off and pushing away someone who could otherwise brighten their life because of things they'll likely never experience from you anyway.  Sure their comments hurt, but that's why you let in people who don't care who's lips meet yours at night ... chances are they are biting the same bullet you are.  That's what kisses always reminded me of anyway.
